name: Cable Bend Radius
blurb: minimum bend radius and clearance for a cable
intro: The minimum inside bend radius of a cable as a multiple of its outside diameter (or thickness, for flat cables and flex PCBs), fixed or flexing, and the room a bend takes: depth behind a panel for a 90° turn and the width of a U-loop. Multipliers are the usual values of BS 7671, TIA-568, IPC-2223 and cable-maker datasheets; your cable's datasheet always wins.

inputs.label: Outside diameter (or thickness for flat / flex)
Straight length before the bend
inputs.help: From the connector, gland or clamp to where the bend starts.

examples.title: 8 mm control cable leaving a panel gland
Screened Ethernet in a drag chain

usage: Pick the cable type (key such as control, controlScr, chain, utp, stp, coax, fibre, ffc, fpc1, or custom with mult), the outside diameter (thickness for flat cable / flex PCB) in mm, fixed or flex, the bend angle in degrees and the straight length before the bend in mm. It returns the minimum inside, centre-line and outside radius, the cable length in the bend, the depth behind a panel for a 90° turn, the width of a 180° loop and, for flexing, the next drag-chain radius. Use it to leave room behind connectors or to route a harness in CAD.
sources: BS 7671 IET On-Site Guide, minimum internal bend radii of cables
ANSI/TIA-568.2-D and 568.3-D, minimum bend radius of balanced twisted-pair and optical fibre cable
IPC-2223 Sectional design standard for flexible printed boards, bend radius ratios
Lapp ÖLFLEX CLASSIC 110 / 110 CY and igus chainflex datasheets (bend factors), igus E-chain radius list
